facts.claim: Wilsons Promontory, 'the Prom', is the southernmost point of the Australian mainland, in South Gippsland.
The national park covers about 50,000 hectares, with about 130 km of walking trails and a number of campsites; the hub is Tidal River, with a store, visitor centre and camping.
The park entrance is 224 km from Melbourne; it is another 30 km from the entrance to Tidal River.

The seas around the southern end are protected as the Wilsons Promontory Marine National Park, with a smaller marine national park in the north; the marine parks offer some of Victoria's best scuba diving and snorkelling.
Wildlife around Tidal River is used to people: wombats, kangaroos and emus are commonly seen. Wombats are common across much of the park.
The promontory has been a national park, in one form or another, since 1898; its lighthouse at South East Point is the southernmost on mainland Australia.
The area is traditional country of the Gunaikurnai and Boon Wurrung peoples, first occupied at least 6,500 years before European arrival.

experiences: Walk coastal tracks to the southern tip of the mainland
Watch wombats, kangaroos and emus up close
Swim and relax on white-sand beaches
Camp beside Tidal River and the bay
Snorkel or dive in the marine national parks

tips.title: Book camping early
tips.detail: Tidal River has 480 unpowered sites. Bookings are essential for Christmas, January and popular long weekends.

tips.title: Drive carefully at dusk
tips.detail: Animals are on the road around sunset and at night, especially on the 30 km from the entrance to Tidal River.

tips.title: Fuel up before the park
tips.detail: Tidal River no longer sells fuel and its store has inflated prices. The nearest petrol station is at Yanakie.

best_months.rationale: Warm summer weather for beaches, swimming and camping, though Christmas and January are the busiest; March is quieter. Wikivoyage's climate section is empty so this is general guide consensus, UNVERIFIED against a fetched source.

seasonal_tags: Christmas and January school holidays are the camping peak (Wikivoyage, bookings essential).

facts.claim: Melbourne (Naarm in Woiworrung) is Australia's cultural capital and second-biggest city, noted for Victorian-era architecture, museums, galleries, theatres, parks and gardens.
The city has about 5.4 million people and the largest urban tram network in the world.
The World Heritage-listed Royal Exhibition Building, the Melbourne Cricket Ground and the National Gallery of Victoria are landmarks.
Melbourne has a strong food, wine and coffee culture and a live music scene.
Australian rules football was invented here; the AFL Grand Final is played at the MCG in spring, the Australian Open is in January and the Australian Grand Prix in March.
It is a base for Grampians National Park, the Great Ocean Road and Phillip Island's penguin parade.
The climate is notorious for changeability, 'four seasons in one day'; summer averages about 26C by day.

experiences: Wander laneways for street art and coffee
Ride the trams through the city
Eat across the city's migrant cuisines

tips.title: Free Tram Zone
tips.detail: Trams in the CBD Free Tram Zone cost nothing and need no touch-on. Touching on inside it charges a full fare.

tips.title: Pack for any weather
tips.detail: The weather can swing through four seasons in a day, so carry a layer and a rain jacket even in summer.

tips.title: Get a myki card
tips.detail: Trains, trams and buses use the myki card (adult card $6). Daily fares are capped, at $11.00 on weekdays as of Mar 2025.

best_months.rationale: Wikivoyage describes warm summers (Dec-Feb) with possible heatwaves and cool damp winters; mild autumn and spring are general guide consensus, UNVERIFIED against a fetched source. Big events: Australian Open Jan, Grand Prix Mar, AFL Grand Final and Melbourne Cup spring.

seasonal_tags: Recurring events: Australian Open (Jan), Australian Grand Prix (Mar), AFL Grand Final (spring), Melbourne Cup (first Tuesday of Nov).
